name: Grey Room
concept: Drain every hue, then let luminance, letter-tracking and one black pill carry the entire hierarchy.

type.families: Neo-grotesque, tightly set (Inter, Helvetica Now, Söhne). Typography does all the work colour normally would, so the family must be good at small sizes.
type.hierarchy: Display 40/44 semibold at -0.03em · section 22/28 medium · body 14/21 regular · micro-caps 10/12 semibold ALL-CAPS at 0.14em tracking. The gap between display and body is deliberately extreme.
type.usage: Tracked-out ALL-CAPS micro-labels are the primary wayfinding device — use them for every section, column and group. Two-tone headlines (first clause in `--ink`, second fading to `--muted`) are the signature move. Never introduce a coloured word.

tokens.texture: Surfaces differ by only a few luminance points — `--bg` against `--surface` is a 3% step, and that step *is* the border. Use shadow sparingly (`0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / .05)`) and hairlines only where a luminance step would be ambiguous. Absolutely no hue: if a value has saturation, it does not belong.
tokens.layout: Generous and quiet, or dense and quiet — never loud. 8px scale, 24-32px section padding, 12px radius on panels, 999px on pills. The single black pill button is the only high-contrast object on the page and should appear at most twice per screen. Role and status chips are whisper-tints of ink, never colour.

best_for: products that must not compete with user content
collaboration tools where avatars supply the only colour
avoid_for: anything requiring strong brand colour recall

image_recipe.template:
[SUBJECT: describe the subject in one clause — e.g. "a stack of shipping containers", "a single ceramic cup", "an abstract network of nodes"]

Rendered as monochrome studio photography or greyscale 3D render.

STYLE — apply all of the following, they are not optional:
- strictly greyscale — zero saturation anywhere in the frame
- soft even studio lighting with gentle falloff, light grey seamless background
- matte surfaces, no gloss or specular hotspots
- one subject centred with generous empty space
- subtle luminance separation between subject and ground rather than hard edges

NEGATIVE SPACE: At least 40% of the frame must be empty light-grey ground.

DO NOT INCLUDE: any colour or colour cast, neon, harsh shadows, busy backgrounds, text or logos in the image, high contrast blacks.
